messages:
maria_chen: ALB -> edge-nginx 502s in ap-southeast1 observed ~09:12 UTC. Canary failing and customer reports. Anyone else seeing health checks flapping?

oncall_jess: Yup seeing target group go Unhealthy in LB console around 09:13. No recent deploys on edge service.

sam_connors: I did push a kube-proxy tweak earlier but should only affect pod networking. Can we capture LB->target flow or check NACLs?

infra-bot: alert: alb/edge-tg unhealthy (unhealthy_count=3) at 2026-03-18T09:13:15Z

adrian_irwin: Jumpbox quick check: `curl -v http://10.10.45.22:80` -> connect timeout. Ran tcpdump on node handling traffic: saw incoming SYN from 3.120.75.99:40002 -> node:80 and a bunch of DENY-to-NODE in VPC flow logs.

sam_connors: I remember we added a 'restrict-ephemeral' NACL yesterday for eu/ap subnets to lock down high ports. Can someone confirm which NACLs are attached to the LB subnets?

maria_chen: Checked console: that NACL (nacl-0c9d...restrict-ephemeral) is attached to the public subnets that host the ALBs in ap-southeast1. Looks like its deny rule for 32768-65535 is before the allow rule.

oncall_jess: That matches: ALB health checks originate from ephemeral source ports. If the NACL denies those source ports inbound on the target subnet, the health checks will be dropped.

sam_connors: Pulled VPC flow log snippet: `Version=2; srcaddr=3.120.75.99; dstaddr=10.10.45.22; srcport=40002; dstport=80; action=REJECT; protocol=6; rulenum=100-deny-ephemeral` — confirm it's the NACL blocking.

adrian_irwin: Quick mitigation options: 1) add explicit allow inbound 32768-65535 for ALB subnets, 2) reorder/remove the deny in that NACL, or 3) move ALB to exempted subnets. Which is fastest?

sam_connors: I'll push an allow rule to the NACL for inbound TCP 32768-65535 from 0.0.0.0/0 with higher priority (lower rule number) to avoid the deny shadowing. Doing now.

deploy-bot: action: update-nacl nacl-0c9d... add-rule allow-inbound-ephemeral 32768-65535 tcp 0.0.0.0/0 (ap-southeast1) — started

infra-bot: alert: alb/edge-tg healthy_count restored at 2026-03-18T09:18:02Z

maria_chen: Confirmed services recovered, canaries green. Root cause: mis-scoped NACL (restrict-ephemeral) attached to ALB public subnets + rule ordering caused health checks to be dropped.

oncall_jess: Follow-up: add a guardrail to our infra-automation to prevent applying that 'restrict-ephemeral' NACL to subnets tagged `role:lb` and add a test that simulates ALB healthcheck flows during NACL changes.

sam_connors: Filing infra ticket and a short postmortem. I'll include the flow log snippet and the exact rule change.

maria_chen: Thanks everyone. Note for runbook: if ALBs show target-group Unhealthy, check NACL rule ordering for ephemeral ranges before doing app rollbacks. :white_check_mark: :party:
